hints.content: **Reflective (or line) symmetry** means that we can reflect a figure across a line, and the figure will remain unchanged.

##Reflection over $y=-x$

This line goes through the midpoints of the parallel sides and the center of the trapezoid. 

Under this transformation, each point on the trapezoid maps to another point which is also on the trapezoid. The trapezoid is *symmetric* over this line.



[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A trapezoid mapped onto a coordinate plane. The x- y-coordinate plane scales by ones. The trapezoid has a point at negative eight, one, a point at negative one, eight, a point at six, negative one, and a point at one, negative six. The equation y equals negative X is graphed on the coordinate plane. Dotted lines show the location of the image trapezoid after being reflected over the graphed line. The image points map onto the current pre-image points.

hints.content:
##Reflection over $y=-7x+1$

Under this transformation, some points on the trapezoid map to another point which is no longer on the trapezoid. The trapezoid is *not symmetric* over this line.



[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A trapezoid mapped onto a coordinate plane. The x- y-coordinate plane scales by ones. The trapezoid has a point at negative eight, one, a point at negative one, eight, a point at six, negative one, and a point at one, negative six. The equation y equals negative seven X plus one is graphed on the coordinate plane. Dotted lines show the location of the image trapezoid after being reflected over the graphed line. The image points are outside of the current pre-image trapezoid.

hints.content:
The symmetries that apply to the trapezoid are:

Symmetry | Applies to the figure?
:- | :-:
Reflective symmetry over the line $y=-x$ | Yes
Reflective symmetry over the line $y=-7x+1$ | No
